chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman from Hafs ibn Ghiyath said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Regarding a man who caught the Friday prayer, when the people were crowded, and he said Takbir with the Imam and bowed, but could not prostrate. The Imam stood up while the people were in the second rak'ah, and this man stood with them. The Imam bowed, but he could not bow in the second rak'ah due to the crowding, yet he was able to prostrate. What should he do? Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the first rak'ah, it is complete up to the bowing. Since he did not prostrate for it until he entered the second rak'ah, that was not permissible for him. When he prostrated in the second [rak'ah], if he intended that this prostration was for the first rak'ah, then the first rak'ah is complete for him. When the Imam gives the Taslim, he stands and prays one rak'ah, prostrating in it, then he recites the Tashahhud and gives the Taslim. And if he did not intend that that prostration was for the first rak'ah, then neither the first nor the second is valid for him, and he must prostrate two prostrations and intend that they are for the first rak'ah, and after that there is a complete second rak'ah in which he prostrates.'
Hafs said: I asked Ibn Abi Layla about it, and he neither struck at it nor came close to it [i.e., gave a precise ruling].

He said: And I heard some of their freed slaves asking Ibn Abi Layla about Friday prayer, whether it is obligatory upon the woman, the slave, and the traveler. Ibn Abi Layla said: Friday prayer is not obligatory upon any one of them, nor upon the one who fears [for his safety].
The man said: What do you say if one of them attended Friday prayer with the Imam and prayed it with him? Will that prayer suffice for him in place of the Dhuhr of his day? He said: Yes.

The man said to him: How can that which Allah did not obligate upon him suffice for that which Allah did obligate upon him? And you have said that Friday prayer is not obligatory upon him, and whoever Friday prayer is not obligatory upon, the obligation upon him is to pray four [rak'ahs]. And the meaning necessitated by you is that Allah obligated four upon him, so how did two rak'ahs suffice for him? Along with what is necessitated that whoever enters into that which Allah did not obligate upon him does not suffice for him from that which Allah obligated upon him. Ibn Abi Layla had no answer to this, and he asked him to explain it to him, but he refused.

Then I asked him about that, and he explained it to me, saying: The answer to that is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, obligated upon all believers and female believers, and granted concession to the woman, the traveler, and the slave that they do not attend it. When they attended it, the concession fell away, and the first obligation became binding upon them, and for that reason it sufficed for them.
I said: From whom is this? He said: From our Master, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the time of the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Friday is until his saying 'and the minimum that should be between the two congregations.' The explanation of all of that has passed fully. Then he said: And the minimum that should be between the two congregations is three miles, and there is no congregation except with a sermon and an Imam. And this report does not contradict the report we mentioned earlier that it is permissible for the congregation to be without a sermon, because that report is construed upon the case where if he prays four rak'ahs, it is permissible for him to combine them without a sermon. And this report applies to the one who prays two rak'ahs, and the one who prays thus is not sufficed except with a sermon.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who misses bowing or prostration in Friday prayer due to crowding?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of joining a congregational prayer late (*masbuq*) under conditions of physical obstruction, specifically addressing the validity of prostration as a substitute for bowing. It further integrates a juristic debate on whether Friday prayer becomes obligatory for those initially exempt (women, slaves, travelers) upon their attendance, a ruling traced back to Imam al-Sadiq via Ibn Abi Layla. The text concludes by clarifying the minimum requirements for a valid Friday congregation, emphasizing the necessity of a sermon (*khutbah*) and imam, while distinguishing it from simple congregational prayer.
